facts.statement: Barcinosuchus is an extinct genus of carnivorous crocodile-like reptile from the early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Barcinosuchus (meaning "Cerro Barcino Formation's crocodile") is an extinct genus of carnivorous metasuchian from the early Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: This peirosaurid lived during the Aptian to Albian stages of the early Cretaceous in what is now Chubut Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: It is a peirosaurid which lived during the early Cretaceous period (Aptian to Albian stage) in what is now Chubut Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The species is known from a single holotype specimen consisting of a skull, lower jaw, and postcranial bones.
facts.quote: It is known from the holotype MPEF-PV 3095, which consists of skull, mandible, and postcranial remains.

facts.statement: Martín Leardi and Diego Pol named the genus and its type species, Barcinosuchus gradilis, in 2009.
facts.quote: Barcinosuchus was named by Martín Leardi and Diego Pol in 2009 and the type species is Barcinosuchus gradilis.

facts.statement: Barcinosuchus lived between 113.2 and 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Barcinosuchus belongs to the family Peirosauridae.
Barcinosuchus is classified as a reptile.
